Process_Text.original: Numerical representations of 3D electrode microstructures are generated by randomly inserting spherical CAM and SE particles into a cubic simulation domain (V_Box). A discrete element method (DEM) implemented in the open-source package LIGGGHTS was used to simulate the pressing process. Granular contact walls were placed at the bottom and all four vertical boundaries of the box. A flat surface was applied at the top and moved downward until the system reaches 200 MPa. Pressure was then held constant until static equilibrium.
Process_Text.simplified: DEM simulation using LIGGGHTS: random insertion of spherical CAM/SE particles into cubic domain, pressing to 200 MPa with Hertzian contact potential, held until static equilibrium.

Equipment.Note: open-source DEM simulation package for pressing process

Boundary_Conditions.Top: flat surface moving downward at prescribed velocity
Boundary_Conditions.Note: Hertzian granular contact potential for normal and tangential interactions and damping forces

Model_Size.Note: Box size L_max ≈ 15 × D_max; L_min ≈ 10 × D_max for convergence

Numerical_Control_Params.convergence_criterion: kinetic energy decayed to zero (static equilibrium)

Simulation_Text.original: A discrete element method (DEM) implemented in the open-source package LIGGGHTS was used to simulate the pressing process. Granular contact walls were placed at the bottom and all four vertical boundaries. A flat surface applied at the top moved downward at a prescribed velocity until 200 MPa. Hertzian granular contact potential used for normal and tangential interactions and damping forces. Pressure held constant until static equilibrium.
Simulation_Text.simplified: DEM via LIGGGHTS; pressing to 200 MPa; Hertzian contact; convergence when kinetic energy → 0.

Simulation_Metadata.Note: Simulation focuses on ionic percolation in cathode composite. CAM particle is 'active' if at least one Li percolation pathway connects it to bulk SE layer.

Structure_Text.original: 3D electrode microstructure with spherical CAM and SE particles. Ionic percolating paths connect CAM particles to the composite cathode/bulk SE interface through SE particles only. Li-ion diffusion in SE much faster than in CAM, so only Li-ion percolation through SE considered.
Structure_Text.simplified: Spherical CAM/SE particle composite. Ionic percolation through SE network determines CAM utilization. Active CAM = connected to bulk SE via SE percolation path.

Structure_Text.original: Percolation in cathode composite consistently improves as f_CAM decreases (SE weight fraction increases) and as λ increases. Percolation always significantly worsens for λ < 1. For f_CAM = 80 wt%, increasing λ from 1 to 3 doubles θ_CAM from ~30% to ~60%. For f_CAM = 85 wt%, increasing λ from 1 to 8 only slightly increases θ_CAM from ~16% to ~20%.

Process_Text.original: Composite cathode fabricated by first hand-mixing LZO-coated NMC particles and LPS for ≈10 min, then mixing for another ≈10 min after adding 5 wt% CNFs. Cell assembled using custom-made pressure cell with PEEK cylinder (8 mm inner diameter) and stainless-steel current collectors. Bulk LPS (35 mg) compressed under ≈100 MPa. Cathode composite (≈5 mg) spread and compacted under ≈200 MPa. In metal (8 mm) attached as anode, ≈200 MPa applied. Cell sealed and cycled under ≈5 MPa (spring).
Process_Text.simplified: Hand-mixing NMC+LPS 10 min → add CNF, mix 10 min → press. Bulk LPS 35 mg at 100 MPa → cathode ≈5 mg at 200 MPa → In anode at 200 MPa. Cycled under 5 MPa (spring).

Equipment.Note: analytical field-emission SEM for particle size estimation
PEEK cylinder with 8 mm inner diameter, stainless-steel rods as current collectors

Processing.Note: Cell fabrication in Ar-filled glovebox (H₂O < 0.1 ppm, O₂ < 0.1 ppm). D_SE = 8 μm LPS prepared by wet ball milling.
